# `Q-9-8` — Invalid Attribute Value

> A CSL attribute's value is not one of the allowed options.

## What this means

Many CSL attributes accept only a small fixed set of values.
`form` on `<cs:date>` accepts `numeric` or `text`; `font-style`
on a styling element accepts `normal`, `italic`, or `oblique`;
and so on. This error fires when the attribute value does not
match any of the allowed options. The message names the element,
the attribute, the value found, and the values that were
expected.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo in the value** (`itlaic` for `italic`).
- **A value from a different CSL version** that has been
  renamed or removed.
- **An English word that resembles a CSL option** but is not
  the exact accepted spelling.

## How to fix

Replace the value with one of the allowed options shown in the
message. If you are not sure which option to pick, the CSL
specification documents the meaning of each accepted value for
every attribute.

## Related

- `Q-9-7` — the attribute is missing entirely.
- `Q-9-10` — an unexpected element in this position.
